messages.author: e511f911cbbb2bd0
messages.subject: Help with (leave one out) cross-validation script
parts:
Dear colleagues,
I'm trying to test the correct classification of 6 species of rodents based on GM data. To do so I've obtained  tables of  (leave one out) cross-validation for my dataset. However, I am not sure if I am applying correctly the usage of LDA.
I used two options. One differs from the other only in adding the argument CV=True at prep.lda function. But this produced an error when I run the predict() function.
Thanks in advance for any suggestion.
Additionally, I would take the opportunity like to ask if to correctly apply LDA I have necessarily split my data into training and test samples? My doubt is because I don't have any unknown individual.

Best regards

Julio


library(geomorph)
library(MASS)
#Option 1
fit.model <- procD.lm(coords ~ log(Csize)*species, SS.type = "III",
                                data = gdf, print.progress = FALSE)
lda.args <- prep.lda(fit.model)
LDA <- do.call(lda, lda.args_dor)
scores <- predict(LDA_dor)
table(lda.args$grouping, scores$class)# Here I use the output of predict

#Option 2
lda.args <- prep.lda(fit.model, CV= TRUE) # CV  is the only different argument I added in this option
LDA <- do.call(lda, lda.args)
scores <- predict(LDA_dor)# output is an error
Error in UseMethod("predict") : no applicable method for 'predict' applied to an object of class "list"

# However anyway I could obtain a similar result cross-validation table
table(lda.args$grouping, LDA$class) # here I use the output of do.call

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Help with (leave one out) cross-validation script
parts:
Julio,

 

I suggest that you follow the example in ‘predict.lda’ exactly. This is an RRPP function, not a geomorph one, which means an extra step is to first convert your 3D array into a 2D matrix (using two.d.array). Then, the help file of ‘predict.lda’ can be used exactly.

 

The ‘predict’ function in MASS is used when you have additional data not used in the training set for the LDA. If one does not have that, then the table classification (as found in the help file mentioned above) is the procedure to use.

 

Dean

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Help with (leave one out) cross-validation script
parts:
Dear Julio,

I think Dean did mean either prep.lda for the RRPP library or predict.lda for the MASS library.  The predict.lda function does exist, but in the MASS library.  The prep.lda function merely prepares either an lm.rrpp or procD.lm fit to use with the lda function (you do not need to use lm.rrpp in place of procD.lm — either works fine).  Once the lda function is used, then the help files for the MASS library should be consulted for options for functions to use with lda objects.

In consulting the help file for the lda function, it is pointed out that an lda object is created only if CV = FALSE, otherwise a list is created.  You can only use the predict.lda function on an lda object; if CV = TRUE, the result is not an lda object.

Whether this is logical, uninformative, confusing, or a mistake, it is unfortunately the domain of the authors of the MASS library  (whom you might contact to inquire why predict.lda cannot be used if CV = TRUE).  Alternatively, realize that your two options to not compete with each other.  The first could be used to calculate discriminant scores; the latter could be used to get a classification table based on cross-validated (jackknifed) posterior probabilities.  If CV= FALSE, there will be a tendency for groups to appear more distinct that they might be because the same data are used to train the model and estimate posterior probabilities — this is considered a circular reasoning problem.  In other words, do not make a table if CV = FALSE but feel free to use this option to get scores.  I think the reason you cannot get scores if CV = TRUE is because rather than one set of vectors, there are n sets of vectors for the n times a single subject is left out.  So there is not a unique set of scores.  This could maybe be better explained with an error statement, but it makes sense why this is a dead-end.

Best,
Mike

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Help with (leave one out) cross-validation script
parts:
Julio,

Just one word of caution.  The posterior probabilities should be more informative than a classification table made from them.  The issue with classification tables is that they make binary decisions based on potentially ambiguous information.  For example, let’s say that a subject from group A could classified as A, B, or C, and the posterior probabilities are:

A B C
0.34 0.33 0.33

This subject would be correctly classified but can one be confident its classification is good?  Alternatively, what if a second subject had the following posterior probabilities?

A B C
0.47 0.48 0.05

This subject would be misclassified as group B even though the probability it is from group A is stronger than the previous subject.  These results (along with others) might demonstrate that groups A and B are similar, even if both are distinct from C, but there might be some subjects that simply cannot be easily classified.

Something like box plots or violin plots of posterior probabilities might be helpful in addition to or in place of classification tables, since they do not require forcing the results into binary variables.

Best,
Mike
